facts.text: "I am still working out the whole hero thing. Lunch I can handle, so pass the dumplings."
facts.why: Miles never says this. It is in quote marks and signed Miles Morales, so it reads as a film line. The closest real piece of advice is Peter B. Parker's line to Miles.
facts.fix: One thing I know for sure: don't do it like me. Do it like you. (sign it Peter B. Parker)

facts.text: the safe house under Aunt May's shed
facts.why: Attached to Aunt May's pancakes. The page I read says the safe house is Aunt May's home, where the other Spider-People shelter. It does not mention a shed. I could not confirm the shed.
facts.fix: the safe house at Aunt May's place

vibe.verdict: A decent Brooklyn school lunch, but the grey canteen look misses the comic book colour and graffiti of the film.
missing: Miles's leap of faith off the building (the cue)
Spider-Ham saying that's all, folks (the safe house)
Peni Parker and her robot SP//dr (the safe house)
Spider-Gwen rescuing Miles and Peter in the forest (the forest)
Peter B. Parker, tired and out of shape, training Miles (the warehouse)
The Prowler and Uncle Aaron on the roof (Miles and Aaron)
ideas: Swap the made up Miles note for Peter B.'s real advice line and sign it Peter B. Parker.
Swap 'Bodega cookies' for 'Spider-Ham's pig in a blanket, that's all, folks'.
Swap 'Coconut milk coquito' for 'Aunt May's hot chocolate for the whole safe house'.
Recolour the lunchroom with halftone dots and graffiti tags instead of plain grey.
